result.markdown: --- title: "R Installation" image: "/images/biostats.jpg" date: "2025-03-21" format: html: fig-align: center page-layout: article toc: true toc-depth: 5 toc-expand: true crossref: custom: - kind: float reference-prefix: "Exercise B.1." key: tabset space-before-numbering: false --- ::: {.cell} ::: ## Download and install R - Download R from the official website: [Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN)](https://cran.r-project.org/). - Select the appropriate version for your operating system (Linux, MacOS, or Windows) and follow the installation instructions. ## Download and install RStudio - Although R can be used as a standalone program, however, it is recommended to use an integrated development environment (IDE) such as RStudio to have a better user experience. - Download RStudio from the official website: [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). ::: {.callout-note style="color: #0466c8;"} - There are other available IDEs such as [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/), [Jupyter Notebook](https://jupyter.org/), and [Positron](https://positron.posit.co), but I personally prefer RStudio for its user-friendly interface. ::: ## Rstudio interface ### Panes - When you open RStudio, you will see FOUR main panes: 1. **Console pane**: This is where R commands can be typed and excuted in an interactive manner. It is also where the output of the commands is displayed. 2. **Source pane**: This is where R scripts or R Markdown documents can be written and edited. Codes in this pane can be also executed in the console pane. 3. **Files/Plots/Packages/Help pane**: This pane can be used to navigate files, view plots, manage packages, and access help documentation to different functions and packages. 4. **Environment/History pane**: This shows all objects in the current R session, as well as the command history. - The pane size can be adjusted by dragging the borders between them. - The pane layout can be customized by going to `View` > `Panes` > `Pane Layout`, where the position of each pane can be modified based on personal preference. ### Running commands in RStudio - To run a command directly in the console, type the command and press `Enter`. - The `<` symbol indicates the prompt where you can start typing any command. - The digit inside the square brackets `[1]` indicates the index (position) of the first element in the output. - To run a command from a script in the source pane, highlight the line(s) of code you want to run then: - press `Ctrl + Enter` on Windows (or `Cmd + Enter` on Mac) to execute the code in the console pane. - click the `Run` button in the source pane to execute the code in the console pane. - Alternatively, you can run a command from a script in the source pane by placing the cursor at any point in the line of code you want to run and then press `Ctrl + Enter` (or `Cmd + Enter` on Mac) or click the `Run` button in the source pane to execute the code in the console pane (this method can only execute one line of code at a time). ## Add your comments
